Competitor News.title: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud
Competitor News.summary: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud NetsDaily
Competitor News.copy:
Barclays Center looked different when Brooklyn Nets fans arrived for Opening Night Wednesday, their first game since look on April 9. On one level, it’s part of yet another upgrade at the arena but on another level, it’s different. It’s not just brick-and-mortar improvement at entrances, better ingress and egress or a new club (or two.) It’s about art and cloud technology and an immersive in-house experience to pull fans away from the comfort of their own home and into the Nets own space.

Some of it is temporary, some is permanent but all of it was quite visible … and visual. The most noteworthy addition is temporary, but will make appearances throughout the season, but it certainly qualifies as art. The Nets 60th anniversary court, dressed up in ABA colors, was striking and it included a feature that blew a lot of minds. Around the edges of the court were the names of all 575 players who ever donned one of the Nets many uniforms going back to the New Jersey Americans. There was Brook Lopez who holds the career record for points as well as Wenyen Gabriel who played one game as a COVID replacement.

bullets: McDonald's has decided not to renew its FIFA World Cup sponsorship, ending a 32-year run when the current deal expires this year. McDonald's CFO Ian Borden said in August that its largest-ever World Cup marketing push "underperformed versus our expectations". bullets: Allianz has secured the naming rights to an LA28 venue in Long Beach, which will be known as Allianz Beach Arena. The Comcast Squash Center at Universal Studios is the only other temporary venue sold so far, while Honda Center and Intuit Dome keep their names during the Games. Wider Sports News.title: Experts call for alcohol sponsorship ban after Scotland World Cup exposure study
Wider Sports News.summary: Experts call for alcohol sponsorship ban after Scotland World Cup exposure study The Herald
bullets: Academics at the University of Stirling, Dr Richard Purves and Dr Catherine Best, have called on the Scottish Government to consider comprehensive restrictions on alcohol sports sponsorship. Their study, funded by Scottish Health Action on Alcohol Problems (SHAAP), analysed 30-second broadcast intervals across Scotland's World Cup matches and found alcohol advertising in almost a quarter of them. Alcohol branding was more prevalent during the matches themselves than in commercial breaks.

SHAAP chair Dr Alastair MacGilchrist said viewers saw alcohol branding around every two minutes, and that self-regulation has not protected children and young people. He urged the government to set out restrictions and a timetable in its alcohol harm prevention plan, due this year. He cited France, which has banned alcohol sports sponsorship for more than 30 years, and noted that most Scottish Premiership clubs have alcohol-industry sponsors or partnerships.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Leading academics have called upon the Scottish Government to consider comprehensive restrictions on alcohol sports sponsorship, after a study revealed the extent to which young people and children were exposed to alcohol advertising during Scotland’s World Cup campaign.

The research, which was funded by Scottish Health Action on Alcohol Problems and undertaken by Dr Richard Purves and Dr Catherine Best of the University of Stirling, analysed 30-second broadcast intervals across Scotland matches, and found that alcohol advertising was present in almost a quarter of them, including frequent exposure to alcohol marketing throughout match coverage.

The African Grand Prix will be held on a new purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, about 40 kilometres south of Kigali and adjacent to the new Kigali International Airport, with tourism board Visit Rwanda as presenting sponsor.

MLB regional broadcast rights are currently worth $1.6bn, according to the latest Ampere estimates, accounting for 43% of the league’s total $3.7bn broadcast rights revenue. Rooted in linear cable, regional sports networks (RSNs) have come under increasing pressure from cord-cutting, as US households move away from traditional pay TV towards streaming.

Over the past four years, 13 of MLB’s 30 teams have lost their regional sports network partners, including 12 following the bankruptcies of Diamond Sports and Main Street Sports Group. This has been exacerbated by the decline in US pay TV, with Ampere estimating a drop in the market from 96 million US pay TV households in 2016 to 65 million by the end of 2026. Meanwhile, streaming households are anticipated to increase from 57 million to 112 million over the same period.

Rugby.title: Tadhg Furlong faces possible four-year ban
Rugby.summary: Tadhg Furlong faces possible four-year ban Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited after Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster on Saturday and could face a ban of up to four years. The 33-year-old is accused of grabbing Munster's Gavin Coombes by the genitals under Law 9.27, which covers acts against fair play. Bans for such offences start at 12 weeks, with the most severe cases carrying up to 208 weeks.

Coombes complained to referee Andrew Brace during the first half. The television match official, Colin Stanley, could not establish what happened from the footage, but the complaint was recorded in the referee's report and reviewed by the citing commissioner. A disciplinary panel will decide the seriousness if Furlong is found guilty. Even a 12-week ban could rule him out of the November Tests and might affect his place in the 2027 Six Nations. South Africa hooker Jan-Hendrik Wessels received a nine-week ban in 2025 for a similar act.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland star Tadhg Furlong could face a ban of up to four years after being cited following Leinster's clash with Munster. The 33-year-old prop is accused of grabbing Munster star Gavin Coombes by the genitals.

Rugby.summary: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong is cited over an alleged groin grab in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster on Saturday.
bullets: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab during Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday. Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace in the 37th minute, but television match official Colin Stanley found no video evidence at the time. Furlong has been cited under Law 9.27, and the URC said disciplinary arrangements would be announced in due course.

If found guilty, the 33-year-old could miss Ireland's Nations Championship matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa in Dublin, plus the finals weekend in London. South Africa's Jan-Hendrik Wessels received a nine-match suspension in October 2025 for a similar offence, after a 12-week ban was reduced by three weeks. A comparable sanction would also rule Furlong out of Leinster's Champions Cup pool match with Sale and the festive derbies with Ulster and Munster.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster on Saturday. Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation against an unnamed Leinster player with match referee Andrew Brace in the closing stages of the first half at the Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find any video evidence at the time.

However, experienced front row Furlong has now been cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says a "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

Rugby.copy:
Springbok back-rower Kwagga Smith, 33, will likely see out the remainder of his career at the Bulls after signing a three-year deal with the Pretoria-based team. Smith’s signature has long been rumoured and now the Bulls have confirmed the versatile double World Cup winner is joining them.

Bulls coach Johan Ackermann said he was delighted to team up again with Smith, having coached him previously at the Lions. “As a youngster, he showed character and fight and integrity. He’s a team man who has grown into a stalwart, and it’s been a privilege to watch his career unfold and establish himself as one of the best backrows in world rugby. Wherever he goes he makes a difference, and I look forward to him contributing both on and off the field.”

Rugby.summary: Townsend names Scotland squad with one new face for Nations Championship Scotland Rugby News
bullets: Gregor Townsend has named a 37-man Scotland squad for the Nations Championship northern series, featuring games against New Zealand, Australia and Japan at Murrayfield and the finals weekend at Twickenham. Former Scotland U20 cap Ollie Leatherbarrow, a 24-year-old back-row who has started the season well for Newcastle Red Bulls, is the only uncapped player.

Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson, prop Ollie Blyth-Lafferty, flanker Freddy Douglas, veteran lock Grant Gilchrist and Magnus Bradbury miss out, and Glasgow fullback Josh McKay is not included despite becoming eligible on residency grounds. British & Irish Lions Huw Jones and Blair Kinghorn return, and Duhan van der Merwe is named despite leaving Edinburgh's match after 18 minutes. Tiatia called the tackle dangerous and said Paea's condition would be assessed medically.

World Rugby confirmed a few weeks ago that knee-drop tackles will be outlawed from 1 November. The change forms part of a wider effort to reduce dangerous contact, and World Rugby has also confirmed that the hip-drop tackle is to be removed. Tiatia, a former New Zealand international, pointed to the NRL's strict approach to the technique, while the tackle on the 32-year-old Paea remains permitted under the current laws.

Rugby.title: Munster's Coombes backed after making groin grab allegation

bullets: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan has backed number eight Gavin Coombes, who alleged he was grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck late in the first half of Saturday's 24-18 United Rugby Championship defeat at the Aviva Stadium. Coombes raised the matter with referee Andrew Brace, but TMO Colin Stanley found no video evidence of the incident.

McMillan said he backs his players "100%" when they make such allegations and that it was now for "the powers that be", referring to the citing commissioner, who can review incidents retrospectively. Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said he did not see the incident and called it a "serious matter" for the citing commissioner. He added that Coombes appeared to change his mind midway through the accusation, and that he could see nothing himself.
Rugby.copy:

Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace, but the television match official (TMO), Colin Stanley, could not find any video evidence of the incident. Speaking after the game, McMillan backed Coombes and, referencing the citing commissioner who can punish retrospective incidents after a review, said it was something that had to be left "for the powers that be".

bullets: Leinster came from 13-0 down to beat Munster with a bonus-point win in the United Rugby Championship derby at the Aviva Stadium. Munster led through a Shane Daly try and eight points from 20-year-old fly-half Charlie O'Shea. Tommy O'Brien then scored before half-time from a Jamison Gibson-Park pass. Second-half tries from Ryan Baird and Charlie Tector put Leinster ahead, and Jamie Osborne's late score secured the bonus point.

Ben O'Connor crossed in the final minute to earn Munster a losing bonus point. Gibson-Park, one of 11 British and Irish Lions in Leinster's starting line-up, made three try assists. Leinster travel to Connacht on Friday (19:45 GMT) and Munster host the Sharks at Thomond Park on Saturday (17:30). The two sides' internationals then enter Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures.

However, Tommy O'Brien hit back for Leinster before half-time after being set up by fit-again scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park, who notched three try assists in an eye-catching display.

Rugby.title: Six-try Ireland beat South Africa in Cape Town
Rugby.summary: Ireland score six tries to beat South Africa in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town.
bullets: Ireland beat South Africa with six tries in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town, marking their first trip to South Africa. Aoife Dalton, Linda Djougang and Jane Clohessy scored in the first half to give Ireland a narrow interval lead, with Beibhinn Parsons, captain Erin King and a second Djougang try following after the break.

Ireland lost their WXV opener to the United States before beating Japan, and will aim to finish the campaign with a third win from four games when they meet South Africa again in Cape Town on 31 October (13:00 GMT). The sides' only previous meeting was a 2006 Women's Rugby World Cup match in Canada, which Ireland won 37-0. Ireland made 13 handling errors, but fly-half Dannah O'Brien's goal-kicking proved the difference in the first half.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland scored six tries to mark their first trip to South Africa with victory over the Springboks in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town. Aoife Dalton, Linda Djougang and Jane Clohessy crossed to give Ireland a slender half-time lead at the end of a ding-dong opening period in which Aseza Hele, Vainah Ubisi and Maria Tshiremba scored for the hosts.

Beibhinn Parsons and captain Erin King - who was sin-binned in the first half for a high tackle - extended Ireland's lead in the second half before Lerato Makua hit back for the Springboks.

Rugby.summary: Top rugby match halted for serious incident as player consoled by team-mate AOL.co.uk
Rugby.copy:
The WXV Global Series fixture between Japan and Wales was brought to a halt during the second half following a serious injury sustained by Freya Bell. Proceedings were suspended for over six minutes, with medical personnel from both sides treating the Wales player on the field at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo. At 52 minutes and with Wales ahead 7-0, centre Bell collapsed clutching her leg following a clear-out at a ruck.

Play initially carried on around her as she remained on the ground gripping her leg in visible distress, with a Wales medic attending to her. The referee subsequently called a stoppage, allowing Bell to receive treatment.

Rugby.copy:
The Fiji Water Flying Fijians produced a courageous and disciplined performance to defeat Japan 34–28 in a thrilling international Test match, overcoming the challenge of playing 20 minutes with 14 men to secure a memorable victory on Japanese soil.

In a contest that was evenly poised at 21–21 at halftime, Fiji demonstrated resilience, tactical discipline and composure under pressure to outlast the Brave Blossoms and deliver a winning start for newly appointed head coach Jake White.

Rugby.title: Wales grind out frustrating WXV win against Japan
Rugby.summary: Wales earn a three-try victory against Japan in tricky Tokyo conditions to secure a second win of their WXV campaign.
bullets: Wales beat Japan in Tokyo to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign, in swirling wind, rain and humidity between the sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world. The first half looked likely to end scoreless until scrum-half Seren Lockwood scored in the 35th minute to give Wales a 7-0 lead at the break. Replacement Kelsey Jones drove over from a lineout, and Lockwood added a second try at the death.

Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury during the match. The report described the performance as far from impressive, but said Sean Lynn's side had shown they can win ugly, with the bench making the difference. The two sides meet again in Kumagaya City next Saturday.
Rugby.copy:
Wales ground out a win over Japan in tricky Tokyo conditions to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign. Swirling wind, rain and humidity made for a real battle between sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world, with a scrappy first-half looking likely to end scoreless.

But scrum-half Seren Lockwood's 35th-minute snipe gave the game a much-needed spark and the visitors a 7-0 advantage at the break. Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury, but the impact of the bench proved the difference as Kelsey Jones drove over off a lineout ball, before Lockwood finished a rare moment of class at the death.

Rugby.title: No panic for England but Mitchell issues PWR warning
Rugby.summary: A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses, their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run ended, and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016 - England are not invincible.
Rugby.copy:
Before England's three-match series against Canada, few would have predicted this outcome. A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses; their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run – stretching back nearly four years – ended; and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016.

Over the past 13 months, Canada have turned a 33-13 defeat in the World Cup final into a statement 31-22 win in Ottawa. And three years out from the 2029 World Cup, they have laid down an early marker of their title credentials.

Rugby.title: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement
Rugby.summary: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement The Guardian
bullets: England's Red Roses lost 31-22 to Canada in Ottawa in the WXV Global Series, their first consecutive defeats in a decade and only their third loss in 74 matches. Canada captain Sophie de Goede, the reigning world player of the year, scored a hat-trick, and Savannah Bauder also crossed. England replied through Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Emma Sing, having trailed 12-7 at half-time.

England captain Meg Jones said the team is 'not broken, we just need to grow'. Head coach John Mitchell criticised the lack of a connection between referee Aurélie Groizeleau and the television match official. England finish the WXV series against the USA next Friday, while Canada's next games are slated for the 2027 Pacific Four tournament.
Rugby.copy:
History-makers, era-enders, giant-slayers. Breaking England’s unbeaten run was a statement for Canada last Friday but they backed it up in a 31-22 win to deal the Red Roses their first consecutive loss in a decade, sending a formidable message to the rest of world rugby.

Some may view it as too early to call but Canada are serious contenders for the World Cup trophy in 2029, especially if they progress at the same rate that their performances have improved in just a year from that World Cup final loss to England in 2025.

Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl said the club hope Faletau will be fit after the November break for the Nations Championship. He has played only 31 times for Cardiff since joining from Bath in 2022, and was left out of Wales' Nations Championship squad, with Taine Basham recalled instead. Rugby.title: Canada inflict back-to-back losses on England
Rugby.summary: England suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade as Canada win 31-22 in Ottawa, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede.
bullets: England lost 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa, their first back-to-back defeats in a decade. Canada scored five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick from captain Sophie de Goede. It followed Canada's 24-21 win in Toronto last weekend, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run, and gave Canada a 2-0 series win after a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September.

Head coach John Mitchell said England had become "a little bit predictable" and need a "new stimulus" in the new year. He also called for improved officiating standards after there was no television match official connection in the stadium, saying Jess Breach's disallowed interception try was a turning point. England face the USA in New Jersey next Friday, hoping to avoid three straight defeats for the first time since 2013.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach John Mitchell said England need a "new stimulus" after losing 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa to suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade.

The hosts ran in five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede, as they backed up last weekend's 24-21 win in Toronto, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten streak, with another statement victory.

Rugby.title: Impressive Gloucester beat Bath to extend lead at top of Prem
Rugby.summary: Gloucester storm to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display.
Rugby.copy:
Gloucester stormed to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display. The Cherry and Whites were down to 13 men for a period of the first half but led 9-5 at half-time, having repelled wave after wave of Bath pressure on their tryline.

George Barton then kicked three successive penalties to put the hosts 9-0 up before Kepu Tuipulotu pulled a try back just before the break from a driving maul. Freddie Thomas scored under the posts to stretch Gloucester's lead further midway through the second half and Max Llewellyn had Kingsholm raucous when he rolled over with two minutes to go for a famous victory that reaffirms their status as league leaders.

Rugby.title: Wade equals Ashton's Prem try-scoring record as Newcastle beat Sale
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade equals Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle post their first league win of their season against Sale.
bullets: Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Premiership try-scoring record with his 101st try, scored in the right corner nine minutes into the second half. Newcastle Red Bulls beat Sale Sharks 17-3 at Kingston Park for their first league win of the season, with hooker George McGuigan adding a second try from a maul just after the hour.

The result was only Newcastle's fifth win in four Premiership seasons and leaves Harlequins as the only side yet to win this season. Sale, unbeaten in their previous two league games, scored only a George Ford penalty in blustery conditions. Newcastle coach Dan McFarland said there was no turning point and called it a long journey, adding that Wade deserves to take the record.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle Red Bulls posted their first league win of their season against Sale Sharks. On a blustery night dominated by kicking, penalties and stubborn defence, the match delivered a 17-3 win for the hosts and the try that Kingston Park wanted, with Wade going over in the right corner to draw level with Ashton nine minutes into the second period.

Rugby.title: All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams undergoes life-saving surgery
Rugby.summary: All Blacks legend Sonny Bill Williams undergoes life-saving surgery Ruck.co.uk
bullets: All Blacks great Sonny Bill Williams, 41, has revealed he had open-heart surgery in Melbourne after doctors found a serious heart defect. He disclosed this in a 24-minute YouTube video titled My Heart Stopped. Doctors warned that his heart had grown to 7.5cm and was at risk of rupturing. Surgeon Dr Michael O'Keefe confirmed a Ross procedure to replace his aortic valve, and the operation was successful.

Williams said the recovery was frightening, describing the second day as the point when he thought he would not make it, and he suffered hallucinations afterwards. Doctors believe the condition may have affected his sporting career for years, and he said he had struggled with fitness from his late twenties. He won 58 Tests for New Zealand between 2010 and 2019, and two Rugby World Cups. He also won NRL titles in 2004 and 2013, played sevens at the 2016 Olympics and won the WBA International heavyweight title in 2013.

The Red Roses face Canada again at TD Place in Ottawa on Friday in the third and final Test against them in the WXV Global Series, and then play the USA on 30 October. Talling said England let themselves down in finishing the pressure they built, and that Canada have developed, citing the pace of their backs in the wide channels. Rugby.copy:

Last weekend, Canada brought England’s impressive 41-match unbeaten run to an end, as they claimed a thrilling 24-21 victory at BMO Field in Toronto in front of a record-breaking crowd of 18,621 spectators.

For Morwenna Talling, who made her Red Roses debut in 2020 against Italy in a 54-0 win and has been a regular feature in the squad ever since, the defeat marked a rare low in an England career largely defined by success, but she is determined to help England bounce back when the two sides meet again in the WXV Global Series this weekend.

bullets: Leicester Tigers fly-half Billy Searle, 30, turned down a potential return to France to stay at Welford Road, having agreed a new three-year deal in September. He joined from Agen for the start of 2025-26 and has previously played in France with Toulouse in 2022, Biarritz and Agen. He said he had interest from France but made clear to the club that his priority was to stay.

Searle said staying keeps him in contention for a first full England cap, to add to his England A appearance against Ireland in February. He cited informal conversations with head coach Steve Borthwick and noted that 2027 is a World Cup year. Tigers host Prem champions Northampton Saints on Saturday (15:05 BST) at a sold-out Welford Road, the first meeting since Saints won last season's semi-final on the way to the title.
Rugby.copy:
Leicester Tigers fly-half Billy Searle turned down a potential return to France to "push his game on" at Welford Road and stay on the radar for full England honours in the near future.

Searle, 30, agreed a new three-year deal in September, having joined Tigers from French club Agen for the start of 2025-26. The former Bristol, Wasps and Worcester Warriors stand-off has had three spells playing French rugby in his career - a short stint at Toulouse in 2022, and with second-tier Biarritz and Agen - before moving back to England.

Rugby.title: 'He's been our star performer at training': Duhan van der Merwe back for Edinburgh in poignant Lions clash
Rugby.summary: The Scotland wing aims to put 18 months of injury hassles behind him when he plays his first game of the season for Edinburgh on Friday.
bullets: Scotland wing Duhan van der Merwe, 31, will play his first game of the season for Edinburgh against the Lions in the URC at Hive Stadium on Friday, after 18 months of injury problems that began with an ankle injury in March 2025. He had ankle surgery to be available for last year's British and Irish Lions tour of Australia, scoring five tries in five non-Test games, and was limited to 11 Edinburgh games last season.

Head coach Sean Everitt said Van der Merwe has trained exceptionally well, but that it is too soon to discuss international selection before Scotland coach Gregor Townsend names his squad on Monday for the November Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan. Darcy Graham misses the game with a calf strain. The match follows the death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, from natural causes the day before their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland wing Duhan van der Merwe will aim to put 18 months of injury hassles behind him on Friday when he plays his first game of the season for Edinburgh in their URC match against the Lions at Hive Stadium.

The 31-year-old has endured a challenging time with fitness and form since suffering an ankle injury in March 2025. Van der Merwe had surgery on his ankle in order to be available for last year’s British and Irish Lions tour of Australia, but was never in serious contention for the Test matches despite five tries in five other games he played.

Rugby.title: Former Scotland Rugby International Tim Visser to Stand Trial on Rape and Abuse Charges
Rugby.summary: Former Scotland Rugby International Tim Visser to Stand Trial on Rape and Abuse Charges Ruck.co.uk
Rugby.copy:
Former Scotland rugby international Tim Visser is set to stand trial after being accused of rape and abusive behaviour towards a woman. The 39-year-old faces four charges relating to alleged incidents between 2010 and 2024.

Two charges allege that Visser raped the woman on various occasions. He also faces allegations of threatening, controlling and abusive behaviour. The charges include claims of physical violence and controlling aspects of the woman's daily life.

Rugby.title: Three ex-All Blacks and Sevens star named in Samoa's Nations Cup squad
Rugby.summary: Head coach Tusi Pisi has handed a handful of All Blacks places in his 30-man Manu Samoa squad for the November leg of the World Rugby Nations Cup, with fixtures against Zimbabwe, Portugal and Spain on the horizon.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach Tusi Pisi has handed a handful of All Blacks places in his 30-man Manu Samoa squad for the November leg of the World Rugby Nations Cup, with fixtures against Zimbabwe, Portugal and Spain on the horizon.

The headline inclusions are former All Blacks Akira Ioane, Josh Ioane and Shaun Stevenson, who are among eight uncapped players selected for the campaign. All three qualify for Samoa through heritage and were cleared by World Rugby’s eligibility regulations earlier this year, opening the door to an international switch after previously representing New Zealand.

Rugby.copy:
The Springbok Women will face Ireland for the first time in 20 years with a reshuffled front row following injury to captain Babalwa Latsha. Co-head-coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have moved Xoliswa Khuzwayo to tighthead prop, and named Sanelisiwe Charlie at loosehead prop. Anushka Groenewald retains her spot at hooker.

Replacement loosehead prop Yonela Ngxingolo is in line to earn her 50th cap and will be just the second player to reach that milestone. Lindelwa Gwala and Thandile Mazwi will also offer front-row support from the bench.

Rugby.summary: Exeter sign forward Andre Goedhals from South African side Pumas.
Rugby.copy:
Exeter have signed forward Andre Goedhals from South African side Pumas. The 22-year-old, who is English-qualified having been born in Devon, moves to Sandy Park having helped Pumas reach this year's Currie Cup final and has also spent time with Stormers.

Goedhals can play at lock or in the back-row and has agreed a deal that runs until the summer of 2030. "We've been looking at back five options for a little while now, just because I think it's an area we can still keep developing and improving," Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter told BBC Sport.

Rugby.title: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso stood down with immediate effect
Rugby.summary: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso stood down with immediate effect Ruck.co.uk
bullets: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will miss Exeter Chiefs' match this weekend as he continues to recover from a hamstring injury suffered against Newcastle Red Bulls at the start of the month. He also missed Exeter's defeat to Toulouse last weekend. England hold his EPS contract and have a say in his medical management, and have opted for a cautious approach ahead of the autumn internationals.

Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter said the 23-year-old has been running at decent speed but will have a re-scan at the weekend to decide the next step. Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations with a hamstring problem and started all three of England's Nations Championship matches over the summer, scoring against Fiji and Argentina. England face Australia, Japan and New Zealand before the finals weekend at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.copy:
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will miss Exeter Chiefs’ match this weekend as he continues his recovery from a hamstring injury. The England winger was expected to return after picking up the problem against Newcastle Red Bulls at the start of the month.

However, with the Nations Championship approaching, a cautious approach has been taken to avoid risking further damage. Feyi-Waboso also missed Exeter’s defeat to Toulouse last weekend, as he continued his rehabilitation. His absence has now extended beyond the initial expectations surrounding his recovery.

Rugby.title: Wallabies back Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on wing for first Bledisloe Cup Test against All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Wallabies back Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on wing for first Bledisloe Cup Test against All Blacks The Guardian
bullets: Australia coach Les Kiss has named a settled side for the first Bledisloe Cup Test against New Zealand at Eden Park on Saturday, keeping Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the left wing rather than restoring him to midfield. Queensland Reds centre Isaac Henry, 27, is the only change, starting at outside centre because Hunter Paisami is banned for four weeks for a high tackle against South Africa. Len Ikitau moves to No 12 after passing an ankle fitness test.

The All Blacks are without fly-half Richie Mo'unga, who tore a calf muscle and will miss both Tests, and winger Fehi Fineanganofo, who failed concussion tests. Coach Dave Rennie moves Damian McKenzie to No 10 and names Beauden Barrett at fullback, with Scott Barrett starting in the second row. The Wallabies are looking to end a 40-year Eden Park drought, and Kiss is unbeaten in his first five Tests, with four wins and a draw.
Rugby.copy:
Australia coach Les Kiss called up rookie Isaac Henry and retained star back Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing in a settled team named Thursday to face New Zealand. Four-Test Queensland Reds midfielder Henry will start at outside centre in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park on Saturday, two months after making his debut against Japan in Osaka.

The return of 27-year-old Henry is the only change to the starting side who upset South Africa 42-38 in Perth two weeks ago. Inside centre Hunter Paisami received a four-week ban for a high tackle against the world champions and is not available.

Rugby.title: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens
Rugby.summary: Maro Itoje seals England future by agreeing new deal with Saracens The Guardian
bullets: Maro Itoje has agreed a new deal with Saracens, believed to run until 2029, rejecting interest from Top 14 clubs, with Perpignan and Bordeaux among those mooted. His existing contract, signed in 2024, was due to expire after next year's World Cup. The 31-year-old, who has 102 caps, first played for the club in 2013.

Saracens' Brendan Venter, back in charge for a second time, said Itoje had agreed terms with the owner and described him as a brilliant leader. Itoje was rested for England's summer Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, and had his first full pre-season with Saracens since 2014. He was among the first players given an enhanced England contract, worth £150,000, in 2024, although none of the existing deals run beyond the World Cup in Australia next year.
Rugby.copy:
Maro Itoje has reaffirmed his long‑term commitment to England, rejecting interest from France by agreeing a new deal with Saracens. Itoje’s existing deal, signed in 2024, was due to expire after the World Cup next year but he has agreed terms with his club despite interest from Top 14 sides. A move to either Perpignan or Bordeaux had been mooted but the 31-year-old is to commit his future to the club he first represented in 2013 with a new deal, believed to be until 2029.

The extension is a significant boost for Saracens, who are in a period of transition with Brendan Venter at the helm for a second time and will enable Itoje, who has 102 caps, to continue his international career. It remains to be seen whether Steve Borthwick will still be in charge of the England side but either the national head coach or his successor is to benefit.

The former world number three won three Grand Slam titles: the 2014 Australian Open, the 2015 French Open and the 2016 US Open.

He beat Novak Djokovic in the finals of the 2015 French Open and 2016 US Open, and Rafael Nadal in the 2014 Australian Open final. He also spent 267 weeks in the top 10, won one Masters 1000 title and 15 other tour-level titles. Wawrinka said he wanted to give everything with no regrets and that at some point you have to close the book, while Djokovic called him a "legend".
Racket.copy:

Former world number three Wawrinka might have lost to Czech opponent Jiri Lehecka in front of passionate home support in Basel on Tuesday, but he did not wave farewell without showing the hallmarks of a stunning career that exceeded expectations.

bullets: Jannik Sinner will begin working with former world No 2 Magnus Norman at the end of the 2026 season, according to a report in The Times. Norman takes over from Darren Cahill, who has been part of the Italian's team since July 2022 and, alongside Simone Vagnozzi, helped him win five major titles. Norman is free to join because Stan Wawrinka retires at the end of this season.

Norman, runner-up at the 2000 French Open, previously coached Robin Soderling to back-to-back Roland Garros finals in 2009 and 2010. He also guided Wawrinka to three Grand Slam titles. Sinner successfully defended Wimbledon this year but has not played since beating Alexander Zverev, because of a knee injury. He missed the US Open and the ATP Finals, will lose the No 1 ranking to Zverev in the coming weeks, and is due to return in early 2027.
Racket.copy:

According to The Times, five-time Grand Slam winner Sinner will start working with former player Magnus Norman at the end of the 2026 season with the Swede taking over from Darren Cahill.

Norman is a former world No 2 who finished runner-up at the 2000 French Open and he has enjoyed great success as a coach, as he mentored Robin Soderling in 2009 and 2010 and during that period his fellow Swede reached back-to-back French Open finals.

Racket.title: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts
Racket.summary: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts BBC
bullets: More than 150 men's doubles players, including British world number one Henry Patten and the Bryan brothers, have signed an open letter urging the ATP Tour to rethink proposals that would cut draw sizes and reduce prize money from 2028. The letter was signed on Monday by 137 current players, 28 legends and 20 national federations. The ATP has proposed halving doubles draws at Masters 1000 events to 16 teams, with smaller tournaments cut to eight teams, and the share of prize money going to doubles could fall from 20% to 10%.

The ATP board, made up of chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives, will vote on the proposals at the ATP Finals in Turin next month. The ATP says the changes are based on data-led analysis of costs, revenue and viewership, and ATP sources insist a compromise is likely. Mike and Bob Bryan said they would support legal action, as in their 2005 lawsuit against the ATP over planned doubles changes.

Racket.title: Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev earn over $1 million each in ATP’s record $18.3 million payout as Novak D
Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev earn over $1 million each in ATP’s record $18.3 million payout as Novak D The Times of India
bullets: Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev were the biggest beneficiaries of the ATP Tour's record $18.3m profit-sharing payout for the 2024 season, each earning more than $1m from Masters 1000 events. The ATP finalised the distribution on 3 October 2025, with 186 players who earned ranking points at the nine events qualifying. Sinner received $1,333,770 and Zverev $1,228,472, ahead of Andrey Rublev on $698,474.

The payout was 2.7 times the $6.6m distributed for 2023, while Novak Djokovic finished 12th with $403,641, outside the top 10. Under the 50-50 model introduced in 2022, profits above base prize money at Masters 1000 events are split equally between players and tournaments. The payments are separate from prize money and the $20.5m fixed bonus pool for the top 30 players.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev emerged as the biggest beneficiaries of the ATP Tour's record profit-sharing payout for the 2024 season, with the two stars earning more than $1 million each from the Masters 1000 events. Novak Djokovic, meanwhile, finished outside the top 10 in the profit-sharing standings despite another productive season on the tour.

The ATP finalised the distribution of its record $18.3 million profit-sharing pool on October 3, 2025, completing the total compensation package for players who competed at Masters 1000 tournaments in 2024. A total of 186 players who earned PIF ATP Rankings points at the nine events qualified for a share of the payout.

bullets: An Se-young won the women's singles title at the Yonex French Open 2026 on Sunday 25 October, beating India's Pusarla Venkata Sindhu 16-21, 21-11, 21-12 in the final at the Arena Grand Paris. The world No. 1 extended her winning streak to 50 matches, claimed a 10th title of the season and secured a third consecutive French Open crown, her fourth overall. She has won 66 of 67 matches this year.

The streak began after a 2-0 loss to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. An played through an injury near her right Achilles tendon, sustained in the Denmark Open final, which medical examinations showed was not serious. She is expected to enter about three more tournaments this year, including the BWF World Tour Finals, and two more titles would beat her own single-season record of 11. She holds 48 career titles, past Susi Susanti's 46.

bullets: Christo Popov won the Yonex French Open 2026 men's singles title on Sunday, becoming the first French player to win the crown and reaching the world No. 1 ranking for the first time in his career. He beat Indonesia's 19-year-old Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah in a three-game final in front of his home crowd. The result is a milestone for French and European badminton.

Popov had lost the French Open final one year earlier. Speaking to Badminton Europe afterwards, he said he was proud to finally win the title and reflected on the injuries and demanding matches he had overcome during the week. He said he loves the game and plays because he is passionate about badminton, and that he still wants to achieve many more things.

After needing more than two hours and three sets to get the better of Li, Krueger – who won the tournament in 2023 – never really got going in the final as Siniakova ran away with the match and the title with the Czech winning 6-1, 6-0 in one hour and eight minutes to secure her sixth WTA singles trophy.

[OSEN=Jeong Seung-woo Reporter] The world ranking remains No. 1. However, it has been a long time since news of a championship victory was heard. Seo Seung-jae-Kim Won-ho pair lost in the quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour France Open (Super 750) men’s doubles held at Arena Bercy in Paris, France, on the 24th (Korean time) to Malaysia’s Goh Jae Wei-Nur Izzudin pair (world No. 5) with a game score of 0-2 (15-21, 18-21).

Racket.title: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign
Racket.summary: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign 조선일보
bullets: The Badminton World Federation announced that An Se-young has set a record by winning her 47th international singles title, passing Indonesia's Susi Susanti, who won 46. The BWF's count covers only titles since 1999, when it began compiling statistics, and excludes team events such as the Uber Cup. An has won nine individual titles this season from 11 tournaments entered.

An has held the world number one ranking for 106 consecutive weeks, 168 in total, with 122,287 points. She has reached the semi-finals of the BWF World Tour France Open (Super 750) in Paris, beating China's Han Yue 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals. A fourth French Open title would be her 10th of the year and the first three-peat at the event since Pi Hongyan won in 2003–2005.
Racket.copy:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Kim Ga-eul] Japan has praised An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), the "world's strongest," for her overwhelming skills. An Se-young is demonstrating formidable strength. She has won nine gold medals in individual events this season alone. Out of 11 international tournaments she participated in this season, she finished as runner-up at the All England Open, March, and withdrew in the round of 16 at the Japan Open, July, due to injury, but she claimed victory in all other events. An Se-young set a new record by reaching the top 11 times last year, tying the all-time single-season record for most wins in men's and women's singles with Kento Momota (Japan). At her current pace, she could set a new record.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) officially announced, "An Se-young has set a new record by winning her 47th international singles title." The previous record was held by Indonesia's badminton "legend" Susi Susanti, who had 46 wins. However, the BWF's count of singles titles only includes records since 1999 when it began compiling statistics. Additionally, team event results such as the Uber Cup (World Women's Team Badminton Championships) or the Asian Team Championships are excluded.

Racket.title: Record 4 Malaysian doubles pairs in French Open semis
Racket.summary: Record 4 Malaysian doubles pairs in French Open semis Free Malaysia Today
bullets: A record four Malaysian doubles pairs have reached the semi-finals of the French Open, a BWF World Tour Super 750 event. Women's world number four pair Pearly Tan-M Thinaah beat Bulgaria's Gabriela and Stefani Stoeva 21-12, 21-15 and next face Japan's Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakashini. Men's world number five pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzudin Rumsani beat world number one pair Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae of South Korea 21-15, 21-18 in 36 minutes.

Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun reached the last four after a walkover, as compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik retired trailing 0-5 two minutes into the first game, with no official reason given. Malaysia has not won the men's doubles title since Gan Teik Chai-Koo Kien Keat in 2004. In the mixed doubles, Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing face China's world number six pair Guo Xin Wai-Chen Fang Hui in the semi-finals.
Racket.copy:
This is a record achievement at the prestigious BWF World Tour Super 750 championships. And history beckons for world No 4 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah, who could add a second title being the only Malaysian women’s doubles pair to have won the crown in the tournament’s 117-year history, in 2022.

In the last eight match early this morning, the Malaysian pair defeated world No 9 pair Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva with a comfortable score of 21-12, 21-15 in a match that took 39 minutes.

bullets: PV Sindhu reached the semi-finals of the BWF French Open in Paris on Friday, beating Chinese Taipei's Chiu Pin-Chian 21-13, 21-14. The two-time Olympic medallist, who won silver at the 2016 Rio Games and bronze at Tokyo 2020, will next face either fifth seed Putri Wardani of Indonesia or Japan's Hina Akechi for a place in the final.

Earlier, Sindhu beat Japan's Riko Gunji 21-12, 21-16 in 44 minutes. Compatriot Ashmita Chaliha, who beat world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi on Thursday, lost 10-21, 21-17, 16-21 to Japan's Nozomi Okuhara in the quarter-finals. Ayush Shetty retired hurt against sixth seed Kodai Naraoka, and Lakshya Sen withdrew before his opening match. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty and Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand both lost in the first round.

Paris, October 23 (IANS) Indian badminton ace and two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu sailed into the semifinal of the BWF French Open, beating Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-Chian 21-13, 21-14 in Paris on Friday.

The Indian made a good start, winning the first game 21-13. She took that momentum into the second game and led 11-2 at the interval. Chiu showed signs of fightback, but Sindhu closed out the win, taking the game 21-14.

Racket.title: Boulter in Japan semis & back as British number one
Racket.summary: Katie Boulter reclaims the British number one ranking after fighting back to beat Antonia Ruzic in three sets in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open.
bullets: Katie Boulter reclaimed the British number one ranking by beating Antonia Ruzic 3-6 6-3 6-3 in the Japan Open quarter-finals in Osaka. The eighth seed, 30, trailed the world number 91 by a set and a break but won eight straight games, reaching her first semi-final since Queen's in June.

She will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in the last four and, whatever the result, will climb above Sonay Kartal and back into the world's top 50 when the WTA rankings update on Monday. Boulter had been overtaken on Monday after Kartal's run to the final in Wuhan, a 55-point gap. She plays in Tokyo and Hong Kong in the coming weeks, while Emma Raducanu looks unlikely to return this season because of the shin injury that ruled her out of Wimbledon.
Racket.copy:

The 30-year-old was dethroned on Monday following Sonay Kartal's run to the final in Wuhan but knew she could overturn the 55-point deficit by reaching the last four in Osaka.

Eighth seed Boulter trailed world number 91 Ruzic by a set and a break but recovered to win 3-6 6-3 6-3 in two hours to reach her first semi-final since Queen's in June. She will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in the last four and whatever the result will climb above Kartal and back into the world's top 50 when the WTA rankings are updated on Monday.

bullets: India's Ashmita Chaliha beat third seed and 2025 World Championships gold medallist Akane Yamaguchi 21-19, 21-18 in the second round of the French Open to reach the quarter-finals. Chaliha, who won the Korea Masters earlier this year, had lost to Yamaguchi in the Denmark Open round of 16 last week, and had beaten China's Han Qian Xi 21-18, 24-22 in round one.

She will face either 11th seed Pornpawee Chochuwong or Nozomi Okuhara in the last eight. Ashmita, who had beaten China’s Han Qian Xi in a 21-18, 24-22 first-round thriller on Tuesday, beat Yamaguchi in yet another close match, winning 21-19, 21-18. She recovered from 1-5 down in the first game and 5-9 down in the second, having beaten Denmark's Amalie Schulz 21-6, 21-4 in the previous round.

Paolini, a two-time Grand Slam finalist, broke early to take a 3-1 lead before Jovic found her rhythm. The American teenager broke twice to win the opening set 6-4. Jovic moved two breaks ahead at 4-1 in the second set, but Paolini fought back to cut the deficit to 4-3. Jovic held serve before breaking again to close out a 6-4, 6-3 victory in 1 hour, 22 minutes.

Racket.copy:
ATP Safe Sport prevented more than 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players and fans across ATP and player social media channels during the past year, helping protect the tennis community from online abuse.

Delivered in partnership with Tennis Data Innovations (TDI), sports technology company Sportradar, Social Protect and Arwen AI, ATP Safe Sport was launched in 2024 as part of the ATP's broader commitment to player welfare. Croft told Sky Sports Tennis that movement is central to Raducanu's game and must be fully recovered.

Martin Kaymer has confirmed he has gone under the knife for his second operation in the space of two months. The big German, who memorably sank a six-foot putt at Medinah Country Club to complete a miracle comeback for Europe at the 2012 Ryder Cup, revealed on 18 September that he had shoulder surgery after a "challenging year".

The FT said another group including Dustin Johnson may sign up once they reach agreement with the Saudi PIF over severance payments on their original contracts. Golf.title: Why European legends are still banned from the Ryder Cup – despite turning their back on LIV Golf
Golf.summary: Why European legends are still banned from the Ryder Cup – despite turning their back on LIV Golf Today's Golfer
bullets: A long-standing DP World Tour rule effectively bars Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell from serving as European Ryder Cup captains or vice-captains, and Today's Golfer understands it is not expected to change in the near future, even as several players leave LIV Golf. Introduced in January 2017, the rule says players cannot hold the roles if they decline European Tour membership or fail to meet their minimum event obligation in any season.

Poulter and McDowell have declared themselves out of LIV 2.0 and could regain DP World Tour cards next season through Legends category status, but the captaincy roles remain out of reach. Garcia, 46, says he will return to the DP World Tour "without a doubt" and has told captain Luke Donald he will help as a player or vice-captain at Adare Manor. Justin Rose, Francesco Molinari and Rory McIlroy are now next in line as captains.
Golf.copy:
A number of greats have quit LIV Golf, prompting speculation they could return to the Ryder Cup captaincy fold. But, writes Ben Parsons, there’s still one small problem… Several European legends are joining the exodus from LIV Golf, but it would take a dramatic U-turn at this stage for their Ryder Cup expulsion to be overruled.

TG understands that a long-standing rule which effectively bans the likes of Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell from representing Europe as captains or vice-captains, is not expected to be changed in the near future to accommodate the returning greats.

Golf.title: LIV Golf lurches forward to uncertainty
Golf.summary: LIV Golf lurches forward to uncertainty Global Golf Post
bullets: LIV Golf is moving towards a restructured "LIV 2.0" amid bankruptcy proceedings. The Financial Times reported that about 15 players have tentatively committed. The plan, funded by private-equity firm BC Partners, offers players equity and is expected to feature 10 events next year with significantly reduced prize money. The league has not held an event since August and has none scheduled.

Cameron Tringale, Richard Bland, Brendan Steele, Ben Campbell and Victor Perez have publicly pledged to LIV. Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter, Tom McKibbin and Graeme McDowell have said they will not return. Sergio García has been freed by the bankruptcy court to leave, and Jon Rahm's separation agreement awaits final approval. Mark King, former TaylorMade chief executive, has joined as a senior advisor. Dustin Johnson is seeking money he says the PIF owes him, and Bryson DeChambeau's decision is seen as pivotal.
Golf.copy:
Instead, we are left to reading transcripts of bankruptcy proceedings, lawyer statements and social-media posts as LIV Golf lurches toward whatever the future holds for what is being pitched as a reimagined entity even if the league’s primary drawing cards – name-brand players – are evacuating as if the fire alarm has gone off.

If this is ultimately leading to the end of LIV, it’s not surprising that it is not as quick and clean as the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund’s sudden announcement earlier this year that the money hose had been turned off. Terminations invariably involve red tape and hurt feelings.

Golf.title: Which Big Names Are Missing The 2026 Abu Dhabi Championship?
Golf.summary: Which Big Names Are Missing The 2026 Abu Dhabi Championship? Golf Monthly
bullets: Several leading players will miss the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the penultimate event of the 2025-26 DP World Tour season, scheduled for 5-8 November, with the DP World Tour Championship following on 12-15 November. Ryder Cup players Matt Fitzpatrick and Robert MacIntyre are not in the field, nor are Ryan Fox, Shane Lowry, Justin Rose, Ludvig Aberg and Alex Fitzpatrick. Rory McIlroy and Jon Rahm are among those entered.

Fitzpatrick, the defending DP World Tour Championship winner, said in September that he was not comfortable playing in the Middle East given the ongoing war in the region and the birth of his child in August. MacIntyre said he would wait and see developments before deciding. Min Woo Lee, Si Woo Kim and Ryan Gerard, who sit around 40th to 70th in the Race to Dubai, are also absent, ending their seasons. Marco Penge is focusing on keeping his PGA Tour card and is entered in the Mexico Open instead.
Golf.copy:
After a total of 40 tournaments, just two remain in the 2025-26 DP World Tour season, with the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and DP World Tour Championship left to play. The DP World Tour Play-offs are two of the biggest on the circuit's calendar but, because of the ongoing war and complications in the Middle East, the jeopardy of the two tournaments has been left in the balance.

As of writing, both tournaments are scheduled to take place on the 5-8th November and 12-15th November but, although they will possess high-caliber fields, which include the likes of Rory McIlroy and Jon Rahm, some have opted not to make the journey over to the UAE.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Remains 'On Track' For New Era After Announcing Key Hire
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Remains 'On Track' For New Era After Announcing Key Hire Golf Monthly
bullets: LIV Golf says it remains on track to secure the support it needs for its new era after appointing former TaylorMade chief executive Mark King as senior adviser. King will recruit, build and chair LIV's advisory board. He spent 34 years at TaylorMade, later served as president of Adidas North America and was chief executive of Taco Bell. LIV chief executive Scott O'Neil said King's relationships and expertise would help the league build a sustainable, player-focused global tour.

After securing an initial investment agreement from BC Partners, LIV has tried to retain its 2026 roster for LIV 2.0. At least a dozen players have said they will not sign up and five have publicly committed, with a further 15 reportedly tentatively in. Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are among those leaving. BC Partners Credit's Ted Goldthorpe said the creditors remain confident in progress. A report cited a 30 October deadline to decide whether the restructuring continues or moves towards liquidation.
Golf.copy:
The LIV Golf League says it remains "on track" to secure the support needed to reach its new era after appointing former TaylorMade CEO Mark King as Senior Advisor. King spent 34 years at TaylorMade and helped to elevate the equipment manufacturers into a billion-dollar corporation before departing in 2014.

The University of Wisconsin - Green Bay alumnus also went on to spend time as president of Adidas North America and as the CEO of Taco Bell but may now face his biggest challenge in attempting to lift LIV 2.0 off the ground.

Golf.title: Qualifiers for all 2027 Signature Events, The Players and majors
Golf.summary: Qualifiers for all 2027 Signature Events, The Players and majors PGA Tour
Golf.copy:
For the second time in as many PGA Tour stops, the winner of the tournament generated an exemption into a major that wasn’t up for grabs for just anyone. Michael Brennan turned the trick at the Baycurrent Classic two weeks ago. Then, after the last break of the season, Austin Smotherman replicated the achievement at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship.

Smotherman defeated Seamus Power on the third hole of a sudden-death playoff at Port Royal Golf Course on the western edge of Bermuda on Monday. The final round was banged due to high winds, so the duo returned to the course the next day to decide who would leave the archipelago as the sole survivor. When Smotherman’s third straight par on the par-3 16th clinched victory, he not only secured his second PGA Tour title in as many starts of his own, but he triggered a provision that yielded an exemption into the 2027 U.S. Open.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Appoints Former TaylorMade Executive Mark King as Senior Advisor
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Appoints Former TaylorMade Executive Mark King as Senior Advisor LIV Golf
Golf.copy:
NEW YORK -- October 26, 2026 -- LIV Golf, the innovative global golf league blending world-class competition with entertainment and culture, today announced the appointment of Mark King as a Senior Advisor, effective immediately. In his role, King will leverage his deep roots in professional golf and provide valuable expertise in evolving organizations to help propel transformation as the League works to complete a recapitalization transaction (the “Transaction”) with BC Partners Advisors L.P., the credit business of BC Partners (“BC Partners Credit”), that will bring LIV Golf’s next era to fruition.

King’s appointment comes as LIV Golf remains laser focused on advancing its conversations with players regarding their participation in the go-forward League. With BC Partners Credit’s initial investment secured and the process for player commitments well underway, the League is on track to secure the support needed to complete the Transaction, and planning for the 2027 season is underway. King is expected to recruit, build and serve as Chairman of LIV Golf’s Advisory Board for the next era of the League.

Golf.title: LIV Golf’s collapse leaves the DP World Tour facing a promise it can’t afford to keep
Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s collapse leaves the DP World Tour facing a promise it can’t afford to keep Golf Digest
Golf.copy:
In the moment his week went without a headline. Charles Howell III finished his 54-hole trek around the Old Course, Carnoustie and Kingsbarns one shot on the wrong side of the cut line at the Alfred Dunhill Links earlier this month. No offense to Howell, who has put together a good career, but at 47 his results stopped being notable long ago. Except that performance is newsworthy now, because it appears those rounds were an audition. And that he’s being considered at all has irritated DP World Tour regulars, hinting at a larger mess. LIV Golf has imploded, and the European circuit must sift through the debris without cutting itself.

Interestingly, it is rubble the DP World Tour helped cause. While LIV has had too many self-inflicted wounds to list, what hindsight might consider the nascent league's knockout blow came from the DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings when he announced his league would no longer grant conditional releases to LIV players next year. “Players need to make a choice,” Kinnings told the BBC. “We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour.” LIV golfers could no longer double-dip, and European players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton would lose Ryder Cup eligibility if they did not side with the DP World Tour. In turn, the bulk of LIV’s already-thin roster of formidable players have since signaled their intention to leave.

Golf.title: Former US Open winner McDowell confirms LIV exit
Golf.summary: Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell becomes the latest major champion to exit LIV Golf.
bullets: Graeme McDowell, the 2010 US Open winner, has confirmed he will not pursue a place in LIV 2.0, the new version of the breakaway tour due to start in 2027. The 47-year-old Northern Irishman joined LIV in 2022, and his best finish was a tie for second in Virginia in June 2025. He follows Jon Rahm, Louis Oosthuizen, Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter and Tom McKibbin in leaving.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing in April after investing more than $5bn, and LIV filed for US bankruptcy protection last month. It has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit, but only a handful of players have committed so far. LIV has appointed former TaylorMade and Adidas executive Mark King as senior adviser. A lawyer for the league told a bankruptcy court it would know by the end of October whether LIV 2.0 can proceed or the league will be wound down.
Golf.copy:
Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell has become the latest major champion to confirm his departure from LIV Golf. The 2010 US Open winner, 47, announced on Monday he has "decided not to pursue" LIV 2.0, the new version of the breakaway tour which is due to start in 2027.

Major winners Jon Rahm and Louis Oosthuizen have also confirmed their departures, while McDowell's fellow countryman Tom McKibbin said he was exiting LIV to return to the DP World Tour last week.

Golf.summary: Austin Smotherman claims his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship.
Golf.copy:
Austin Smotherman claimed his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship. The 32-year-old American parred the third extra hole to fend off the Irishman and seal his second tournament win in as many starts after a breakthrough victory in Utah earlier this month.

Smotherman and Power contested the sudden-death play-off on Monday after inclement weather forced organisers to cancel Sunday's scheduled final round. With more bad weather forecast on Monday, officials decided to scrap the final round and proceed with a play-off between the 54-hole leaders.

Golf.title: Bermuda Championship: Austin Smotherman beats Seamus Power in Monday play-off for second PGA Tour win
Golf.summary: Bermuda Championship: Austin Smotherman beats Seamus Power in Monday play-off for second PGA Tour win BBC
bullets: Austin Smotherman won the Bermuda Championship on Monday, beating Seamus Power at the third hole of a sudden-death play-off for his second PGA Tour title, following his first victory in Utah earlier this month. Weather forced the cancellation of the final round, so officials went straight to a play-off between the 54-hole leaders, who were both on 16 under.

Smotherman, 32, shot 65, 66 and 66, while 2022 champion Power had 66, 64 and 67. Power missed a 20-footer on the first play-off hole, the par-three 16th at Port Royal, before Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet at the third. Power's runner-up finish effectively secures his 2027 PGA Tour card: he entered the week 103rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings and is projected to rise to 53rd, with the top 100 earning cards.

bullets: Jon Rahm received $26m from LIV Golf in the year before the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 8 September, court records filed in New Jersey show. Bryson DeChambeau was paid nearly $13.9m and Dustin Johnson $10.7m, while LIV also paid seven executives $15.6m in retention money. Chief executive Scott O'Neil received more than $13.6m between September 2025 and August 2026.

Contractors including Fresh Tape Media ($1.23m), Mobii Systems (over $1.1m) and Deltatre (nearly $860,000) say they are still owed money, and players are among the largest unsecured creditors, with Rahm owed about $7.5m. Rahm has reached a separation agreement releasing LIV from monetary claims, which a judge is due to consider on 5 November. LIV is seeking to relaunch as LIV 2.0 with up to $300m from BC Partners Credit, subject to O'Neil signing enough players by a deadline of 25 October that can be extended.
Golf.copy:

The figures are in documents filed late Thursday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey, where LIV sought Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 8. The payments to players also include nearly $13.9 million to American Bryson DeChambeau, the 2024 U.S. Open champion, and $10.7 million to Dustin Johnson, a former world No. 1. Australian Cameron Smith and American Bubba Watson each received about $2.5 million.

Golf.summary: Yuri Yoshida Wins in Republic of Korea for Her First LPGA Tour Victory LPGA
bullets: Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament at Pine Beach Golf Links in Haenam on Sunday, taking her first LPGA Tour title. The 26-year-old Japanese player finished on 17-under 271, one shot ahead of overnight leader Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi, who both ended on 16 under. Yoshida began the final round four shots off the lead and opened with an eagle at the par-5 second hole.

Ryu led by four strokes going into the final round but shot a 73, and both she and Yoshida bogeyed the 18th. Choi remains without a win in 125 LPGA Tour starts, having held or shared a 54-hole lead five times, and was runner-up in Shanghai the previous week. Defending champion Sei Young Kim tied for 55th. The tour moves to Kuala Lumpur next week for the Maybank Championship, the third of four events in its Asian swing.
Golf.copy:
HAENAM, South Korea (AP) — Yuri Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in a close finish at Pine Beach Golf Links on Sunday. It was Yoshida’s first LPGA Tour victory and came in dramatic finale as both overnight leader Haeran Ryu and Yoshida bogeyed the final hole leaving the Japanese player ahead by one stoke and a four-round total of 17-under 271.

Yoshida was four shots off the pace going into Sunday’s final round but lit up the front nine with an eagle at the par-5 second, followed by three consecutive birdies to be 5-under 31 at the turn. Bogey’s at the 15th and 18th was offset by a crucial birdie at the 17th which gave the 26-year-old the buffer she needed.

Golf.title: LIV Golf paid executives $15.6 million as vendors went unpaid, while Cam Young signed intent with LIV new bankruptcy filings show
Golf.summary: LIV Golf paid executives $15.6 million as vendors went unpaid, while Cam Young signed intent with LIV new bankruptcy filings show Golf Digest
bullets: LIV Golf paid $15.6m in retention payments to executives before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, according to court documents. CEO Scott O'Neil received a $6.375m retention bonus on 24 June and was paid more than $13.6m between 12 September 2025 and 28 August 2026. CFO David Phillips was paid more than $3.3m and chief legal officer John Ruzich about $2.6m, while founding commissioner Greg Norman received more than $9.4m when he left in September 2025.

The payments came as LIV failed to pay vendors, prompting lawsuits including Fresh Tape Media seeking $1.23m and Mobii Systems claiming more than $1.1m. The filings also show Cameron Young signed an intent to play for LIV after the 2022 Open. The deadline for players to commit to LIV 2.0 is Sunday 25 October. A LIV attorney told the court the league expects to know by the end of the month whether it will proceed, with up to $300m of financing from BC Partners.

Just months before, O'Neil received a bonus of about $2.7 million in February. Golf.title: LIV's latest court filings paint clearest picture of league's lavish spending
Golf.summary: LIV Golf's most recent bankruptcy court filings are a reminder of just how much money it takes to run a flashy golf league. The post LIV’s latest court filings paint clearest picture of league’s lavish spending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Bankruptcy filings are notoriously cumbersome, but every bankruptcy judge would admit the tedious paperwork is necessary. If a company is declaring bankruptcy, and thereby seeking some sort of legal protection against its current state, it had better be able to explain why.

But the process of doing so is a nightmare for lawyers as much as it is for their printers. It doesn’t take long for the number of pages to cross the threshold of tens of thousands. On Thursday evening alone, thousands of pages were filed in LIV Golf’s bankruptcy case, across its lot of international entities, its 13 franchises and dozens of other subsidiaries. Staring at it might send you into a daze, but there’s plenty that can be gleaned from these documents, which were prepared by LIV’s management and advisors. Thursday’s trove offered one main theme: LIV Golf owed many companies money.

Golf.title: Race To Dubai Update: Can Casey Jarvis Make It A Four Horse Race?
Golf.summary: Race To Dubai Update: Can Casey Jarvis Make It A Four Horse Race? Golf Monthly
bullets: Eugenio Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship took him above Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed to the top of the Race to Dubai rankings. Casey Jarvis, fourth before the Genesis Championship in Korea, led after day one and could climb to third with a top-two finish, or to second with a win.

Points rise sharply in the closing DP World Tour Play-Offs in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, where the title will be decided. McIlroy is chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, while Reed would become only the second American winner. Jarvis, 23, won the Magical Kenya Open and South African Open early in the season, and Chacarra, a former LIV Golf player, won the KLM Open and Open d'Italia in June.
Golf.copy:
It was supposed to be a two-horse race between big guns Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed before Eugenio Chacarra's surging form saw him muscle in on the act. But that three-way battle could become a four-strong contest heading into the DP World Tour Play-Offs if Casey Jarvis can back-up a fine start at the Genesis Championship in Korea.

After a couple of near misses, Chacarra's victory at the DP World India Championship saw the Spaniard overtake both McIlroy and Reed to climb to the top of the points rankings.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau Confirms DP World Tour Start But Still 'Committed' To LIV Golf 2.0
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau Confirms DP World Tour Start But Still 'Committed' To LIV Golf 2.0 Golf Monthly
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has been confirmed for the Nedbank Golf Challenge at Sun City, South Africa, on 3-6 December, where he will face Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan. It will be his first non-Major DP World Tour start since 2022 and his first competitive action since the LIV Golf finale in August. Gary Player had announced his entry in August.

ESPN has reported that DeChambeau remains committed to LIV Golf and is working to bring LIV Golf 2.0 to life. A 25 October deadline applies for chief executive Scott O'Neil to sign enough players, as a $300m investment from BC Partners depends on the number and quality of signings, although the deadline could be extended. DeChambeau had reportedly spoken to the DP World Tour about more starts next season, but Guy Kinnings has said players must choose one tour or the other.
Golf.copy:
Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his appearance at December's Nedbank Golf Challenge on the DP World Tour, but he is reportedly still focused on helping LIV Golf 2.0 become a reality.

The two-time US Open champion was announced as an entrant for 'Africa's Major' back in August by Gary Player himself - and now the tournament has confirmed his appearance. The Nedbank Golf Challenge in honour of Gary Player will take place at Sun City from 3-6 December where De Chambeau will take on the likes of Justin Rose, Marco Penge and defending champion Kristoffer Reitan.
